review_output: {"summary":"The fixes for the two earlier findings hold: duplicate-message keys are now per account, the browser cookie is checked against the OAuth state before any database read or LINE call, and linking a user also requires that user's current session. The Serializable claim and project switch read and write each other's rows, so the database aborts one of them when they overlap. The migration's NO ACTION deletes, orphan-identity cleanup and partial indexes are consistent. One major issue remains: the webhook route seems able to reach only the vendor's default account, so unfollows from other accounts may never be recorded. Three minor or nit issues remain: switching a project back to its old account permanently blocks re-sends, the in-flight-send check blocks switches too broadly, and a single shared OAuth cookie breaks parallel login flows.","findings":[{"area":"Consent revocation / webhook routing","file":"src/app/api/webhooks/line/[vendorId]/route.ts","severity":"MAJOR","issue":"The only webhook route supplied is `/api/webhooks/line/[vendorId]`, so `params.accountId` is always undefined and `findLineAccount` always resolves the vendor's default account.","evidence":"The handler types `accountId?` in params, but no `[accountId]` segment exists in the supplied routes, and `findLineAccount(db, vendorId, undefined)` filters on `isDefault: true`.","impact":"Unfollow events from a non-default project account fail signature checks with a 401 (or update only the default account), so those identities stay unrevoked and keep receiving pushes; the same happens to the old default's webhook when the default changes.","recommended_fix":"Add an account-specific route, `/api/webhooks/line/[vendorId]/[accountId]`, that passes the explicit account ID through, and show that per-account URL in the account settings.","required_test":"Send a signed unfollow webhook for a non-default account and assert it returns 200 and revokes only that account's identity, while the same body signed with the default account's secret is rejected.","confidence":0.6},{"area":"Delivery idempotency after switching back to an old account","file":"src/lib/line-notification.ts","severity":"MINOR","issue":"If a project switches A→B→A, the delivery suppressed under A still holds A's key, so re-enqueuing the same event through A returns `duplicate` and nothing is ever sent.","evidence":"The suppressed row keeps `(vendorId, lineOfficialAccountId=A, idempotencyKey)`, and `enqueueLineNotification` maps P2002 to `duplicate` without checking the existing row's status.","impact":"After a switch back, buyers who are still linked to account A permanently miss reminder and confirmation messages for those events.","recommended_fix":"When the conflicting row is suppressed with `line_project_account_changed`, re-queue it with a fresh payload instead of returning `duplicate`, or document the switch-back behavior as intended.","required_test":"Enqueue on A, switch to B, process so the row is suppressed, switch back to A, enqueue again, and assert exactly one push goes out through A.","confidence":0.6},{"area":"Project account switch availability","file":"src/app/actions/project-line-actions.ts","severity":"MINOR","issue":"The in-flight check blocks a switch whenever any delivery on the old account is `sending`, including deliveries for other projects, default-account user notices, and stale leases that only clear on the next worker run.","evidence":"The `findFirst` only filters on `vendorId`, `lineOfficialAccountId` and `status: \"sending\"`, with no project/subject or `claimedAt` lease filter.","impact":"On a busy shared account, or after a worker crash, managers keep getting `lineError=unavailable` and cannot change the project's account.","recommended_fix":"Ignore rows whose `claimedAt` lease has expired, and either scope the check to deliveries whose subjects resolve to this project or accept the current, more conservative check and say so in a comment.","required_test":"Seed a `sending` row with an expired `claimedAt` and one belonging to another project, then assert the switch succeeds.","confidence":0.55},{"area":"OAuth browser binding UX","file":"src/lib/line-login-browser-binding.ts","severity":"NIT","issue":"Every flow uses the same fixed cookie name, so starting a second LINE flow in another tab overwrites the first flow's binding.","evidence":"`response.cookies.set(LINE_LOGIN_BROWSER_COOKIE, ...)` always writes the single cookie `celebrate_line_oauth`.","impact":"The first tab's callback fails with a generic `line=error`, although security is not affected.","recommended_fix":"Key the cookie name by a short prefix of the binding hash, or accept the limitation and show a clear 'restart login' message.","required_test":"Start two flows, complete the first, and assert the user sees the documented behavior (a clear failure message or success).","confidence":0.5}]}
